Start every feature, defect or documentation task through [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), then read BOTH [Development Policy](../../docs/policies/DEVELOPMENT_POLICY.md) and [Documentation Policy](../../docs/policies/DOCUMENTATION_POLICY.md). They own scope, approval, native-reference, engineering, test and documentation rules.

Use the policy's exact labeled [required change explanation](../../docs/policies/DEVELOPMENT_POLICY.md#required-change-explanation-2026-10-13)
separately for each individual approval request; follow its meaningful-content requirements, prohibition on bundling
and semantic handoff/root review for delegated work. Correct labels alone are insufficient.

Route migration scope and discovered general defects through the central
[frontend migration boundary](../../docs/policies/DEVELOPMENT_POLICY.md#frontend-migration-boundary-2026-10-13), including delegated work.

For implementation procedures, use the [Development](../../docs/DEVELOPMENT.md), [Architecture](../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), [Testing](../../docs/TESTING_GUIDE.md) and [Database](../../docs/DATABASE.md) guides. For end-user labels/tasks, inspect [canonical Help](../../docs/user-guide/) with the actual views/browser code. This routing aid does not define another workflow or relax any approved decision.
